rows: 31 places · the signature of New York City

rows.w: Cash-and-ticket Lower East Side deli open since 1888, serving 15,000 lbs of pastrami a week under old neon and salami-hanging signs.
Greenwich Village slice institution since 1975, turning out thin, foldable New York-style plain slices from a stand-up counter until the early hours.
Coal-oven pizzeria since 1915 serving whole pies only, no slices, from an 850-degree brick oven in the West Village.
The self-styled 'Sturgeon King' since 1908, a UWS appetizing counter where scrambled eggs come folded with silky smoked sturgeon.
Sourdough bagels that blew up on TikTok, drawing weekend lines so long the East Village shop reportedly faced landlord eviction threats.
Family-run appetizing shop since 1914, slicing smoked salmon, whitefish, and sable behind the counter of a landmark Lower East Side storefront.
TikTok turned its burrata-and-vodka-sauce chicken cutlet hero and square Sicilian slices into a citywide, line-out-the-door obsession.
Billed as America's first pizzeria (1905); the coal-oven clam pie is the one to get.
The cult Nolita slice window; the curled-cup spicy spring pepperoni square draws constant lines.
Nolita red-sauce favorite; the thin-crust tie-dye pie swirls vodka sauce with pesto.
Scarr Pimentel's house-milled-flour slice shop on the LES, a wood-paneled throwback with a modern crust.
East Harlem coal-oven pizzeria since 1933, said to have pioneered the pizza-by-the-slice walk-up counter still working today.

rows.w: Twin reflecting pools sit in the footprints of the fallen towers; the museum below preserves the slurry wall and artifacts.

rows.w: Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse mashing up KBBQ and an American chophouse, grilling dry-aged USDA Prime tableside.
Danny Meyer's Michelin-starred seasonal-American institution; the front tavern room is walk-in and serves its famous burger.
Family-run Ukrainian diner in Little Ukraine since 1954, open late for pierogi, borscht, and potato pancakes.
Kwame Onwuachi's Afro-Caribbean showpiece at Lincoln Center, where day-marinated braised oxtail and curry-goat patties draw long waits.
Michelin-starred ground-floor restaurant in an Art Deco tower; the golden pork katsu is the must-order.
Sourdough bagels that blew up on TikTok, drawing weekend lines so long the East Village shop reportedly faced landlord eviction threats.
1885 Garment District chophouse famous for its mammoth mutton chop, dry-aged steaks, and ceilings hung with thousands of clay churchwarden pipes.
The first U.S. outpost of the Japanese chain, its rich pork-bone broth a benchmark for the city's ramen boom.
Brooks Headley's Bib Gourmand vegetarian burger counter turned sit-down diner, with cult veggie burgers and gelato.
A tiny Michelin-starred Gramercy tapas bar, Costa Brava-inspired, with adventurous plates and a wall of sherry.
Marcus Samuelsson's lively Lenox Avenue dining room serving modern Harlem comfort food like fried yardbird and mac & greens.
Harlem soul-food institution whose menu names dishes for local figures; 'The Rev. Al Sharpton' pairs fried chicken with waffles.

1.45-mile elevated park built on a former freight rail viaduct, running through Chelsea past gardens, art installations, and city views.
The Met's branch for medieval European art in Fort Tryon Park, built from parts of five French cloisters and home to the Unicorn Tapestries.
Greenwich Village square anchored by the Washington Arch and a central fountain, a longtime hub for street performers, chess, and NYU life.
A leafy Flatiron square with rotating public art, dog runs, and the original Shake Shack kiosk under the trees.
